quote: Naturalness measures how natural the poisoned instance reads. As an automatic evaluation proxy, we use a RoBERTa-Large classifier trained on the Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (COLA) to make judgement on the grammatical acceptability of the poisoned instances. Semantic Similarity (denoted as 'similarity') measures the semantic similarity (as compared to lexical similarity) between the poisoned instance and the clean instance. It's measured by the cosine similarity of their sentence embeddings.

We ask five human annotators on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) to classify them into human-written instances and machine-edited instances. For Semantic Similarity, we ask three annotators on AMT to rate on a scale of 1-3 (representing 'completely unrelated', 'somewhat related', 'same meaning' respectively). For Label Consistency, we compare the label annotations of the poisoned instances with the ground truth labels of their clean versions.
